Sky News — published Friday 25 September 2026 07:15 BST

HEADLINE: Electoral Dysfunction: Andy Burnham 'must address immigration' in Labour conference speech, says Harriet Harman

FACTS:
- Harriet Harman, the senior Labour peer, was speaking to Sky News political editor Beth Rigby on the Electoral Dysfunction podcast.
- The Labour Party's annual conference begins on SUNDAY 27 September in Liverpool. Burnham is scheduled to deliver his first keynote speech as party leader and prime minister on TUESDAY.
- It comes days after 781 migrants crossed the Channel in a single day - a new record for 2026 - and the arrival of two migrant boats on British shores that were not detected as they made the crossing.
- The speech also comes weeks after protests in Dover and Portsmouth where masked protesters clashed with police over migrants being brought ashore by Border Force and the RNLI.
- Harman recalled a speech Ed Miliband made to conference as Labour leader over a decade ago, after which he was criticised for failing to mention immigration and the economy.

QUOTE (Harriet Harman, Labour peer, to Sky News): Burnham "absolutely has to" address the issue of migration, otherwise "everybody who wants to make immigration a huge issue" will be saying, "see, he didn't even mention immigration".
QUOTE (Harriet Harman): "So he will need to say something about it."
QUOTE (Harriet Harman): "But I think people do know where Andy Burnham is steering on immigration, but nonetheless he will absolutely have to mention it."
QUOTE (Harriet Harman): "Andy Burnham will know that people will expect him to show that, as prime minister, what he's going to do is control the borders but also control the streets."
QUOTE (Harriet Harman): in the last few days "we've already seen the government coming quite hard on the issue of what are called the uncontrolled crossings", and "absolutely they've got to be clamped down on".
